passages.title: Received gifts lead into a prayer for understanding rather than a claim to rank
passages.summary: The letter opens in Paul’s name to the saints at Ephesus. It blesses God for choosing them in Christ before the world’s foundation. In Christ they have redemption through his blood and forgiveness. God plans to sum up all things in Christ. They were sealed with the promised Holy Spirit, a pledge of their inheritance. Paul has heard of their faith and love and gives thanks. He prays that they will know their hope and God’s power. That power raised Christ and made him head over all things.
passages.uncertainty: The city marker identifies the opening recipient reference. No exact prison, house, or heavenly location is assigned.

lds.text: Doctrine and Covenants 27:13 also speaks of the fulness of times (verse 10). Why does the opening blessing lead into a prayer for understanding?

contextNote.title: Received gifts lead into a prayer for understanding rather than a claim to rank
contextNote.text: Verses 3–14 list gifts already given: choosing, redemption, an inheritance, the Spirit. The prayer in verses 17–19 asks for nothing new to be added. It asks that they see what they have. Verse 18 pictures the heart with eyes that need light. Three things are to be known. The verse names two: the hope of his calling and his rich inheritance. Verse 19 names the third: the greatness of his power toward believers.

passages.title: Former outsiders become members of one household through the removal of hostility
passages.summary: Paul says the readers were dead in trespasses and followed this world’s course. God, rich in mercy, made them alive with Christ. They are saved by grace through faith, so no one can boast. They are created for good works. As Gentiles they were once far from Israel’s covenants and without hope. Christ’s blood brought them near. He broke down the dividing wall and made the two into one new man. Now they are built together into a holy temple.
passages.uncertainty: The city marker identifies the opening recipient reference. No exact prison, house, or heavenly location is assigned.

lds.text: The selected Church lesson applies the building image to Christ, apostles, and prophets. How do good works follow received grace rather than supply a reason to boast?

contextNote.title: Former outsiders become members of one household through the removal of hostility
contextNote.text: Verse 12 lists what the Gentile readers lacked. They were apart from Christ, shut out of Israel, strangers to the covenants. Verse 14 says Christ broke down the wall of hostility. Verse 19 restates their position with the same kind of words. They are no longer strangers and foreigners. They are fellow citizens and members of God’s household. Verse 20 turns household into house, built on the apostles and prophets.

passages.title: The prisoner's task serves shared inheritance and leads into prayer for strength
passages.summary: Paul calls himself a prisoner of Christ Jesus for the Gentiles. A mystery was made known to him by revelation. Earlier generations did not know it as it is now revealed. The Gentiles are fellow heirs and members of the same body. Paul, the least of all saints, was given grace to announce Christ’s riches. He asks them not to lose heart over his troubles. He kneels and prays that they be strengthened and rooted in love. He ends with praise to God, who can do far more than they ask.
passages.uncertainty: The city marker identifies the opening recipient reference. No exact prison, house, or heavenly location is assigned.

lds.text: Why does the speaker ask the hearers not to lose heart over his troubles?

contextNote.title: The prisoner's task serves shared inheritance and leads into prayer for strength
contextNote.text: Verse 3 speaks of a mystery made known by revelation. Verse 5 says other generations did not know it as now. Verse 6 states its content in three words that begin “fellow.” The Gentiles are fellow heirs, fellow members, and fellow partakers of the promise. Each word gives them a full share with Israel’s believers. The means is named at the end: through the good news. Verse 1 shows the cost to Paul: he is a prisoner for these Gentiles.

passages.title: One body needs different gifts and conduct that allows its members to grow
passages.summary: Paul, a prisoner, urges them to walk worthy of their calling. He names one body, one Spirit, one Lord, one faith, and one God. Christ gave apostles, prophets, evangelists, shepherds, and teachers to build up the body. The body is to grow up into Christ, its head. They must no longer walk as the Gentiles do. They are to put off the old man and put on the new. He gives commands about lying, anger, stealing, and speech. They are to forgive each other as God forgave them.
passages.uncertainty: The city marker identifies the opening recipient reference. No exact prison, house, or heavenly location is assigned.

lds.text: The selected Church lesson teaches that different responsibilities strengthen and unify the Church. How does truthful speech protect members of the same body?

contextNote.title: One body needs different gifts and conduct that allows its members to grow
contextNote.text: Verses 22–24 speak of putting off the old man and putting on the new. Verse 25 gives the first plain case, and it starts with “therefore.” They are to put away falsehood and speak truth with a neighbor. The reason is not a rule about lying in general. It is that “we are members of one another.” The phrase recalls the body in verse 16, where each part supplies. A lie between members harms the body both belong to.

passages.title: Shared submission leads into unequal household roles measured against Christ's self-giving love
passages.summary: Paul tells them to imitate God and walk in love, as Christ loved them. Sexual immorality, greed, and coarse talk should not be named among them. They were once darkness and are now light in the Lord. They should use the time wisely and be filled with the Spirit. They should sing, give thanks, and submit to one another. Wives are told to submit to their husbands as to the Lord. Husbands are told to love their wives as Christ loved the assembly. Paul quotes Genesis on two becoming one flesh and calls it a great mystery.
passages.uncertainty: The city marker identifies the opening recipient reference. No exact prison, house, or heavenly location is assigned.

lds.text: The selected Church lesson teaches family care through the Savior's example. How does Christ's self-giving love shape the command to husbands?

contextNote.title: Shared submission leads into unequal household roles measured against Christ's self-giving love
contextNote.text: Verse 21 tells all of them to submit to one another. Verses 22–24 then address wives, and verses 25–33 address husbands at greater length. Verse 25 gives the husband’s part a measure: love as Christ loved the assembly. That love is defined by an act: he “gave himself up for her.” Verse 28 adds a second measure: husbands should love wives as their own bodies. Verse 29 says no one hates his own flesh but feeds it.

passages.title: Household commands lead into shared resistance supported by peace and prayer
passages.summary: Children are told to obey their parents, and fathers not to provoke their children. Servants are told to obey their masters as serving Christ. Masters are told to stop threatening, for they have the same Master in heaven. Paul then tells all to be strong in the Lord. They are to put on the whole armor of God. He names truth as a belt, faith as a shield, and the Spirit’s sword. They are to pray at all times. He asks prayer for himself, an ambassador in chains, and sends Tychicus.
passages.uncertainty: The city marker identifies the opening recipient reference. No exact prison, house, or heavenly location is assigned.

lds.text: The selected lesson teaches care for children and protection through the armor of God. Why does the armor passage lead into prayer for the imprisoned speaker?

contextNote.title: Household commands lead into shared resistance supported by peace and prayer
contextNote.text: Verse 11 says to put on armor against the devil’s schemes. Verse 12 explains who the fight is against, and who it is not. It is not against flesh and blood. That excludes human opponents, even the ones who chained Paul (verse 20). The enemies named are powers, rulers of darkness, and spiritual forces. The armor fits that fight: truth, righteousness, peace, faith, and God’s word. Verse 18 adds prayer for all the saints.

words.label: Covenant
words.meaning: A binding agreement with promises and duties. In the Bible, God makes covenants with people.

words.label: Gentiles
words.meaning: People of nations other than Israel.

words.label: Apostles
words.meaning: People sent out with a message. In the Gospels the word names twelve whom Jesus chose.

words.label: Saints
words.meaning: People set apart as holy. In the letters the word means the believers in a place.

words.label: Assembly
words.meaning: A gathering of people. In the New Testament letters it means a group of believers. Many translations say “church.”

words.label: Circumcision
words.meaning: The cutting of the foreskin. Genesis 17 makes it the sign of God’s covenant with Abraham.

words.label: Redeem
words.meaning: To buy back a person or property. The word is also used for God’s rescue of people.

words.label: Unclean
words.meaning: Unfit to take part in worship until a set cleansing is done. Leviticus 11–15 gives the rules.
